title: Compare multiple test conditions on the same time axis
summary: Validate three synthetic demonstration CSV files, then overlay curves that share the same time samples and acceleration units on one chart.
audience: Python beginners in the automotive field who want to overlay test results from multiple conditions
prerequisites: Have Python 3.12 and a terminal ready. Check the version with python --version.
Extract the entire downloaded ZIP and open a terminal in the folder containing example.py.
Start with the included practice data, then compare the results with the original files.
case_a.csv, case_b.csv, and case_c.csv in the inputs folder are all synthetic demonstration data.
All inputs use time in s, acceleration in m/s^2, and the same time samples.

sections.heading: Align the conditions needed for comparison

blocks.text: To overlay several curves in one chart, time and the vertical-axis units must mean the same thing. This example plots the synthetic demonstration data Case A, Case B, and Case C on common axes of time in s and acceleration in m/s^2. Condition names are read from the condition column in each file.

blocks.title: Please check
blocks.text: All inputs and charts are synthetic demonstration data. Cases A–C do not represent real vehicle settings, and acceleration magnitude is not used to rank them or judge safety.

sections.heading: Prepare the folder and input format

blocks.text: The script reads the .csv files in the inputs folder in name order. There must be at least two files, and each file must contain only one condition. Every row must have six columns: dataset_note, condition, time, time_unit, acceleration, and acceleration_unit.

This example compares only when the time arrays of the files are exactly the same. It stops if the number of samples, the start time, or any time value differs. The chart axis shows the shared unit as m/s².

sections.heading: Prepare the files and run the example

items: Extract the ZIP and check that the input file listed in README.txt is in the same folder as example.py. Do not run the example from inside the ZIP archive.
Run the commands below one line at a time in the folder containing example.py. On Windows, if python is unavailable but py is available, replace python in each command with py -3.12.
After the completion message appears, open the new outputs folder. If outputs already exists, first rename it to keep the previous results, then run the example again.

blocks.text: Installation requires an internet connection. BASE in the code sets the input and output paths relative to example.py, not the current terminal folder.

After checking the time order and units in each file, it checks for duplicate condition names. It compares the remaining arrays against the time array of the first file, and adds lines to one Axes only when all of them match. Sorting, time shifting, interpolation, and unit conversion are not done automatically.

sections.heading: Read the chart and summary CSV

blocks.text: The three conditions are overlaid in outputs/synthetic_comparison.png. outputs/comparison_summary.csv stores the number of samples and the minimum and maximum acceleration for each condition. These numbers are a simple summary of synthetic demonstration data.
At the 0.4 s sample, the values of the three curves are 1.4, 1.1, and 1.7 m/s². The lines in the chart connect the samples; they do not create new measured values between them.

sections.heading: Steps to confirm the axes match

items: Check that Case A, Case B, and Case C in the chart legend match the condition values in the input files.
Check Elapsed time (s) on the x-axis and Acceleration (m/s²) on the y-axis.
Compare the values of the three CSV files at 0.4 s with the chart and the summary table.
In a new practice copy, change one time value in case_b.csv to 0.41. Check that it stops with the message Time samples do not match.
In another new copy, change acceleration_unit to g and check that it stops without converting automatically.

rows: Check the actual units and notation in the exported file.
Check the time order in that file and row.
Check the start time, sampling interval, and missing samples. Do not simply overwrite the times without knowing the cause.
Use a different condition name for each file.
Check that one file does not mix several conditions.
Check that the input files are in the inputs folder.

sections.heading: What the chart alone cannot tell you

items: Even with the same numeric time axis, the trigger or reference time can differ. Check the basis for alignment in real tests separately.
Only exactly identical time arrays are allowed. Approximate matching, resampling, interpolation, and time-delay correction are out of scope.
The code does not judge whether different sensor locations, coordinate systems, sampling filters, or test conditions are comparable.
The sample maximum does not guarantee the true maximum between samples. The chart does not provide pass/fail, performance ranking, or safety judgments.

verification.env: Windows 11 (10.0.26200), CPython 3.12.14 (64-bit). openpyxl 3.1.5, Matplotlib 3.10.8. The libraries used by each example are pinned in requirements.txt.
items: Checked 3 conditions × 6 samples of synthetic demonstration data, and the minimum and maximum values
Checked errors for unit mismatch, duplicate or reversed times, mismatched time arrays, and duplicate condition names
Checked that the original hashes are unchanged, existing outputs are refused, and the PNG is created
limits: Did not assess the comparability of real test conditions, time synchronization, measurement uncertainty, or safety.
